title: Print Bench
sub: Designs made with Claude Code and the claude-3d-printing tools, in their print colours. Turn them, measure them, download them.
foot: Built with tools/print_bench.py from github.com/kalmehdar/claude-3d-printing. Sliced in Orca: real time and grams from OrcaSlicer's command line (tools/slice_stats.py), for a Bambu Lab P1S with AMS and a Snapmaker U1 tool changer. The other grams are a shape estimate, about 20% either way.

models.name: Rack status LED bar
models.for: A whole hardware project: 16 addressable LEDs and an ESP32-C3 on a board designed, routed and checked with Claude in KiCad, behind a printed 1U faceplate with a white diffuser window. Runs WLED. Shown as it prints, face down, with the board on its four standoffs above it.
models.status: Fit first: board not yet ordered; read hardware/led-bar/REVIEW.md
models.material: Faceplate PETG black, diffuser PETG white; the board is made by JLCPCB
models.credit: Designed with Claude: hardware/led-bar (circuit.py, layout.py, case.scad)

models.name: Four-colour test card
models.for: The first print on a new multi-head printer. Every colour borders every other colour once; if the edges stay crisp, purge and retraction are right.
models.material: PETG, four heads: red, blue, white, black

models.name: Calibration kit: pick a number
models.for: Tune a filament without measuring anything. Eight numbered chevrons for pressure advance (pick the crispest V tip), nine numbered tiles for flow (pick the smoothest top), a five-band temperature tower (pick the cleanest bridge), and a half-black, half-white block that swaps heads every layer with no prime tower, to see whether a tool changer needs one. Ask Claude to calibrate a filament and tools/caltest.py prints the real tests, each piece at its own setting; you tell Claude the numbers and it updates the profile.
models.status: Check first: the layout is for looking at; caltest.py builds the printable tests
models.material: Any; PETG shown. The kit uses two heads: black and white
models.credit: Designed with Claude in OpenSCAD (models/calibration-kit.scad); the tests themselves come from tools/caltest.py

models.name: Fit card
models.for: Your printer's real clearances in one short print. Six holes, each 8 mm plus the clearance printed under it, and an 8 mm peg. The smallest hole the peg turns in is your slide fit; the smallest it presses into is your press fit. Tell Claude both and every design after uses them.
models.material: Any, one head; print it in the material you design for
models.credit: Designed with Claude in OpenSCAD (models/fit-card.scad); stored with tools/fit.py

models.name: Insert card
models.for: The right hole for M3 heat-set inserts on your printer, in one short print. Six bosses with pockets from 3.8 to 4.3 mm. Melt an insert into each, then screw a bolt in and out: the best hole is the smallest where the insert sits flush and doesn't turn. Tell Claude the number and every design after uses it.
models.material: Any, one head; print it in the material your inserts go into
models.credit: Designed with Claude in OpenSCAD (models/insert-card.scad); stored with tools/fit.py

models.name: Hinge card
models.for: Three print-in-place hinges, printed flat and already assembled, at gaps of 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 mm. Flex each one gently: the right gap is the smallest that frees with a little force and then swings without rubbing. Tell Claude the number and later hinged designs use it.
models.material: PETG or PLA, one head; print it in the material your hinges will be
models.credit: Designed with Claude in OpenSCAD with BOSL2's knuckle_hinge (models/hinge-card.scad)

models.name: Snap-fit card
models.for: A two-arm clip that clicks through a slot in a plate and comes out with a firm pull, and a living-hinge sample to fold. The arms are sized from the material's strain limit, so a too-short arm is refused in the model, not snapped on the bench.
models.material: PETG, one head (PLA works for the clip; the model leaves the living hinge out in PLA)
models.credit: Designed with Claude in OpenSCAD (models/snap-fit.scad): snap_clip, snap_slot and living_hinge modules

models.name: Colour-coded Gridfinity bins
models.for: Eleven bins that fill a 5 x 5 Gridfinity tray, 42 mm tall, each name printed into a band in its category colour: red power, blue network, white storage, plain black for the rest.
models.status: Ready: prints as two plates, because the set plus a four-colour prime tower overflows a 270 mm bed
models.credit: Designed with Claude in OpenSCAD (models/gridfinity-bin.scad); Gridfinity is Zack Freedman's open standard

models.name: Screw-top jar
models.for: A small jar and lid that print without supports and screw together first time: a 45 degree flank thread, the play from your measured slide fit, blunt thread starts so the lid finds the thread. Set inner_d and inner_h for a bigger one.
models.material: PETG, two heads: black jar, red lid (or one colour)
models.credit: Designed with Claude in OpenSCAD with BOSL2's trapezoidal threads (models/threaded-jar.scad)

models.name: Clip-on cable tags
models.for: One tag per lead end, the colour saying what the lead carries and the ID printed in. Each clip is sized to its own cable, from mains down to slim Cat6: measure yours and set LEADS.
models.status: Fit first: print one tag per cable type and check it snaps on

models.name: Filament swatch card
models.for: One card per spool: its name and the temperatures it printed well at, printed in, plus a 0.4 to 1.6 mm step strip that shows how see-through the colour is. A hole takes a keyring.
models.status: Ready: set swatch_name, nozzle and bed for each spool
models.material: Two heads: the spool's colour, and a contrasting one for the text

models.name: Desk cable clip
models.for: Snaps over a cable and sticks to the desk edge with a 20 x 20 mm adhesive pad. Prints flat, no supports.
models.status: Fit first: set cable_d to your cable's diameter

models.name: Upgrade, before: a plain bin
models.for: Stands in for any STL you downloaded: one colour, no label, no magnets, and no source file to edit.

models.name: Upgrade, after: label, accent rim, magnets
models.for: The same STL upgraded by Claude without its source: M3 SCREWS printed into the front, the top 3 mm of the rim cut off and printed red, and 6 x 2 mm magnet pockets in the base. Turn it over to see the pockets.
models.material: PETG, three heads: black, red, white
models.credit: examples/models/upgrade-bin.scad: import() the STL, then difference, intersection and union
